# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 36 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_036_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 6, Chapter 2 — How to Discern the Two Angels

**1** I asked him, "Sir, how will I know which spirit comes from God and which is diabolical?" **2** "Listen," he replied, "and I will explain both spirits to you so that you can test them on the basis of what I say. **3** The spirit from God is patient, peaceful, modest, abstaining from all wickedness and futile worldly desire, making itself humble before all, quieting itself, not arguing with anyone, not pushing itself forward, nor being overly bold in speech — it speaks through peace and gentleness. **4** This spirit pleases God. When therefore this spirit enters your heart, speak with it on matters of righteousness. For where the Lord dwells he does not inhabit a place of deception; but where God is, there great understanding is present as well. Trust therefore the spirit that comes from God and has power; do not trust at all the spirit from the devil, for it has no power." **5** I asked, "What is the power of the spirit from God, and what is the power of the spirit from the devil?" **6** He replied, "The spirit from the devil has no power at all — it is weak like the grass of winter. It is foolish and untrustworthy. When the earthly spirit has no power it is like a withered winter vegetable and dries up completely. **7** But the spirit from God, which has power in it, is vigorous and strong, upright in character — it is trustworthy and free from all doubt. When this spirit enters your heart, speak with it about righteousness, justice, and holiness."

---

*LOGOS note: "Like the grass of winter" — a striking natural image for the impotence of the demonic: winter grass is brown, dead-looking, easily blown away. The divine spirit, by contrast, is vigorous (zōtikos = full of life).*
